sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Compiler settings
sections.what: Sets how code is read and checked, turns on strict checking, maps @ to a src folder, and lists which files are checked.
sections.why: Likely reason: the default setup for a Next.js and TypeScript project.
sections.watch_out: Narrowing the include list can hide errors in files that are no longer checked.

summary: TypeScript settings that control how strictly the code is checked and which files are included.
purpose: Controls type checking and how the editor understands the code.
why: Likely reason: this is the usual setup for a Next.js and TypeScript project, with strict checks to catch mistakes early.
how: 1. Sets the language target and module style. 2. Turns on strict checks. 3. Maps the @ prefix to a src folder. 4. Lists the files to check. 5. Excludes node_modules.
inputs: None typed directly. Read by the compiler and the editor.
outputs: Type errors and editor hints. No output files are written.
risks: The @ alias points to a src folder that is not visible in this packet. If that folder does not exist, imports using it will fail. Strict mode can produce many errors if changed.
debug: If imports fail with a path error, check the @ alias. If type errors appear after edits, run the build to see them.
